info.desc: "Licensed to Ill" is the debut album by the Beastie Boys, released in 1986. It is the first rap LP to top the Billboard 200 chart. It also peaked at #2 on the Top Hip Hop/R&B Albums chart. It is Columbia Records' fastest selling debut record to date and sold over five million copies. Background Produced by Rick Rubin & Beastie Boys Kerry King of Slayer made an appearance on the album playing lead guitar on "No Sleep 'Till Brooklyn", and appeared in the music video, which is a parody of glam metal. podcast.body: Released on November 15, 1986, this album was a monumental success, becoming the first rap album ever to top the charts. It combined punk, rock, rap, funk, and hip hop into a globally successful formula and featured Kerry King of Slayer on guitar, introducing countless millions, especially white suburban kids, to hip hop. "And of course, things completely exploded with their license to Il Album which came out on November 15th in 1986."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on November 19, 1986, this album was one of the first successful fusions of rap, hip-hop, and rock, appealing to rap, alternative, and mainstream rock fans. Kerry King of Slayer played guitar on the album while concurrently recording *Reign in Blood*. It socially and culturally bridged a huge gap between black and white music fans, who were previously "miles apart." The album became one of the fastest-selling debut albums in history, the first rap record to hit number one on the American album charts, and remains a top-selling back catalog item, selling hundreds of thousands of copies annually. Columbia Records, its distributor for Def Jam, recorded it as their fastest-selling record to that point, eventually selling over ten million copies in the U.S. alone. "Musically, it was one of the first successful fusions of rap, hip hop and rock."

podcast.body: Released on November 19th, 1986, this album was a groundbreaking fusion of rap, hip-hop, and rock, appealing to rap, alternative, and mainstream rock fans. It featured Kerry King of Slayer on guitar, who played during the recording of Slayer's "Reign in Blood." The album bridged the gap between black and white music fans and became one of the fastest-selling debut albums in history, being the first rap record to hit number one on the American album charts. It has sold over 10 million copies in the US and remained a top-selling back catalog item for years, moving at least 500,000 copies annually 10-15 years later. The band initially wanted to title it "Don't Be a Faggot." "Licensed to Ill was the first rap record to ever hit number one on the American album charts."

podcast.body: The Roland TR-808 drum machine is prominently featured throughout the Beastie Boys' first album, with producer Rick Rubin enhancing its sound and layering it beneath the tracks. "The 808 is all over the first Beastie Boys album."

podcast.body: The debut album was initially perceived as a parody of hip hop, leading to the band being pigeonholed as a novelty act for the first eight years of their career. Despite its humorous nature, Rolling Stone magazine acknowledged its significant impact. Profits from this album were later used to fund their G-Sun studio. "License to ill was a parody of hip hop. It was a good one, but it was still a parody."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This 1986 album generated substantial income for the Beastie Boys, selling at least 2 million copies annually in the "olden days" before the collapse of record sales due to streaming. The band received "nice checks" from these sales. "The Beastie Boys saw a nice checks from sales of license to ill because this 1986 record sold at least 2 million every year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album features a gatefold package that unfolds to two square feet (four square feet double-sided) of artwork. The front cover shows the tail of a Boeing 727 with "Beastie Boys" on it and a registration number 3MTA3, which reads "eat me" when held up to a mirror. The back cover depicts the 727 crashed nose-first into a mountain. The design concept of a private jet was developed by Stephen Bierram and World B. Ohms, inspired by stories of Led Zeppelin on their private jet, as described in the biography "Hammer of the Gods." "If you look at the album from the front, we see the tale of a Boeing 727 with Beastie Boys on the tail. The plane has a registration number 3MTA3. But if you hold it up to a mere, it says, eat me."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was a groundbreaking milestone, becoming the first-ever rap record to top the charts and demonstrate that rap and hip hop were enduring genres capable of coexisting with rock music. It served as many white kids' initial exposure to this new, combined sound of rock, hip hop, and rap, and is cited as an inspiration for numerous bands like Korn, Limp Bizkit, and Linkin Park. The album entered the top 40 on December 20, 1986, staying for over nine months, and eventually hit number one in early 1987, where it remained for seven consecutive weeks. "License to ill was the first ever number one hip hop record."
